subject: GPT-6 Astra original 200-game run
assessment: The recorded agent's performance deteriorated substantially after the early period. Very uncertain initial Elo and the rolling 50-rated-game calculation magnified the appearance of a continuous decline. The evidence shows attempted learning without reliable transfer, alongside a substantial reduction in recorded reasoning work during games. The data do not establish which workflow changes caused the deterioration.

rating.method: Independently recomputed using the pinned rating.py posterior. Full-strength games excluded throughout. Provisional engine-relative ratings, not human Elo.
rating.rollingWindowInterpretation: Stronger early results leave a 50-rated-game window gradually. The last two nonoverlapping 32-rated-game comparison samples each scored 39.0625%, supporting a decline to a poorer overall level rather than uninterrupted deterioration at every later game.

matchedComparison.method: 10,000 resamples of complete paired-color opponent rotations. Observational block bootstrap; not a randomised experiment.

reasoningUsage.source: Native token_usage_record metadata; 10,423 unique response IDs, no duplicates; sums verified against final thread cumulative usage.
reasoningUsage.scope: Sum recorded reasoning usage for model responses between each benchmark start and result, normalised by accepted learner moves. Includes in-game overhead; excludes between-game study and separate practice. No reasoning text inspected.
reasoningUsage.settings: Original turn metadata is Max except a brief Medium interval affecting 11 own moves in game 84. The matched late period is Max, so a sustained lower setting does not explain the decline.
reasoningUsage.interpretation: Less recorded reasoning during games is a plausible contributor, but could also reflect changed positions or procedures. This is not causal proof or a measurement of a fixed thinking allowance.

evidence: Procedures addressed changing lines, blockers, pawn origins, recaptures, king safety, opening development and conversion. Trials also changed opening choices and queen-exchange preferences, rather than exclusively adding checklists.
Trial 15 switched White to d4 and Black versus e4 to e6/d5. Trial 16 tested a queen-exchange preference and explicitly discontinued it after continued errors.
Trial 21 passed supplied legality checks and won one practice from a deliberately chosen two-rook advantage, but its other practice lost both rooks and benchmarks 151-156 went 1 win and 5 losses.
Benchmarks 169-174 all passed a narrow first-15-move material-loss screen while scoring only 1 win, 1 draw and 4 losses. Opening-process compliance failed to predict later safety.
Astra's own notes repeatedly acknowledged that known-position correction and legal supplied lines did not establish generalisation.

persistentErrors.finding: Imagined h4xg3 as a White pawn recapture; it is backwards. Lost a rook, then also imagined a rook recapture through its own king.
Promoted c8=Q into referee-confirmed stalemate while a bishop and two pawns ahead. The presumed spare opponent pawn move did not exist.
Bf5 allowed Qxf5 while its own bishop blocked the imagined rook recapture.
Again misstated a rook's pawn defence through an intervening enemy pawn; later surrendered the queen under a king attack.

contextAndInfrastructure.interpretation: Growing history and repeated compaction are possible contributors. They do not independently explain the deterioration: compaction also occurred during the stronger early period, and the active move checklist was shortened.
contextAndInfrastructure.moveToolOutputScreen: No explicit truncation markers found among 3,719 early and 3,727 late observed move-tool outputs. FEN output was commonly present; asynchronous first responses may show only job-admission status. This screen does not certify every output's semantics.
contextAndInfrastructure.finding: No stronger benchmark opponents, node-budget change, corrupted game outcomes or changed rating method were found that explains the deterioration.

limits: One evolving run cannot identify a causal effect of practice, strategy changes, inference allocation or memory. It demonstrates lower recorded performance, not deterioration of the underlying model weights.
